editorial:
Imagine you are planning your dream wedding, but instead of worrying about the flowers, you have to worry about a creepy killer who hates brides. You get to follow a young woman who is not even sure she wants to get married, only to find out she is being hunted by a psycho. The vibe is pure 80s suspense, with a lot of tension and a gritty feel. You also have a tough cop on the case who is dealing with his own past pain, which adds a bit of weight to the story while the body count keeps rising around the main girl.

What really works here is the slow build-up and the way it keeps you guessing who the killer is. The acting is solid for a slasher, and the pacing keeps things moving without feeling rushed. While some of the special effects look a bit dated now, it just adds to the old-school charm. If you love vintage screams and mystery, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick to rent on Apple TV for a movie night, or you could add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you love owning high-quality classics.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the killer is actually the main character's own fiancé. He has been playing the loving partner while secretly murdering her friends. In the final showdown, he tries to kill her too, but the tough cop arrives just in time. After a tense struggle, the killer is finally stopped. You see the bride escape the nightmare, realizing that the man she was supposed to marry was the monster all along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school slasher films and unexpected twists.
